subsystems.name: Body and actuation
subsystems.role: limbs that move like a person's, with enough strength and speed for real work.
parts: structural limbs in aluminium or carbon fibre

subsystems.name: Hands and end effectors
subsystems.role: grasping and manipulating objects of unknown shape and weight.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal
subsystems.role: keeping a mobile machine running for a full shift.

subsystems.name: Perception
subsystems.role: building a usable model of the surroundings in real time.

subsystems.name: Control and learning
subsystems.role: deciding what to do and how to move, without hand-coding every action.

subsystems.name: Fleet infrastructure
subsystems.role: running thousands of machines as one managed system.

subsystems.name: Volume manufacturing
subsystems.role: producing actuators, gears and sensors at automotive-like cost and quality.

buildSteps.title: Fix the task envelope
buildSteps.detail: Decide payload, reach, speed and environment, because every later choice — joint torque, battery size, hand complexity — follows from it.

buildSteps.title: Design the actuators
buildSteps.detail: Each joint is a motor, gearbox, encoder and controller sized together so the machine can lift its own weight plus a useful load.

buildSteps.title: Make the hands
buildSteps.detail: Fingers are built with tendon or linkage drives and fitted with tactile arrays, since hands are the hardest and most failure-prone part.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the body
buildSteps.detail: Limbs, torso, wiring harness, cooling channels and battery are integrated, keeping mass low and centre of gravity stable.

buildSteps.title: Train the control policy
buildSteps.detail: Policies are first learned in simulation with randomised physics, then fine-tuned on real hardware and on data recorded from human teleoperation.

buildSteps.title: Prove safety
buildSteps.detail: Force, speed and pinch limits are set, emergency stops and geofencing added, and the machine certified for working near people.

buildSteps.title: Scale up production
buildSteps.detail: Actuator and sensor lines are automated so unit cost falls toward the price of a car rather than a laboratory instrument.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and maintain fleets
buildSteps.detail: Robots are shipped to sites with charging, servicing and software-update logistics, and their failures feed back into the next design.

prerequisites.why: models that transfer one skill across objects and settings are early; most deployed robots still repeat a fixed motion.
human-level hand control in clutter is unsolved; hands are fragile and easy to jam.
precision motors and reduction gears are costly at the volumes a global fleet would need.
battery energy per kilogram limits how long a strong, fast machine can work.

prerequisites.tech: Safety standards for machines among people
prerequisites.why: rules for a learning, general-purpose robot sharing space with untrained people do not yet exist.
the car and appliance industries already make motors, gears and batteries in the tens of millions per year.

pathway.milestone: single-purpose robots in warehouses, farms and factories
pathway.unlocks: reliable narrow automation and the supply chain it depends on.

pathway.milestone: humanoid and mobile manipulator pilots in logistics and manufacturing, often with remote human help
pathway.unlocks: real operating data from unstructured tasks.

pathway.milestone: foundation models that let one robot learn a new task from demonstration in hours
pathway.unlocks: economical deployment in small batches rather than only huge factories.

pathway.milestone: multi-robot crews doing construction, care and agriculture work
pathway.unlocks: labour where workers are scarce, plus pressure to redesign workplaces around machines.
a large share of physical work done by machines — bounded by battery materials, rare-earth magnets, electricity supply and public acceptance, not by software alone.
